chunks: And from him, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Hakim, from Jamil ibn Darradj, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I heard him (peace be upon him) say: 'The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) designated Zakat upon nine things, and excused (exempted) whatever is besides that: upon silver, gold, wheat, barley, dates, raisins, camels, cattle, and sheep.'
Al-Tayyar said to him, while I was present: 'Indeed, we have a lot of grain called rice.'
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to him: 'And we have a lot of grain.'
He said: 'Is there something due upon it?'
He said: 'No, I have already informed you that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) excused whatever is besides that.'
ai.seo_question: What are the nine specific items upon which Zakat is obligatory according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) explicitly enumerates the nine specific categories of wealth subject to Zakat, establishing a foundational principle in Shia jurisprudence that limits the obligation to these items unless extended by analogy (qiyas) or further evidence. The dialogue regarding rice highlights the scholarly distinction between the Prophet's explicit designation of these nine items and the exemption of other grains, a key point of discussion in the development of fiqh al-Zakat. It underscores the precision with which the Ahl al-Bayt preserved the Sunnah regarding financial obligations.
